glosses: Control or occupancy of something for which one does not necessarily have private property rights.

examples.text: Once complete, guide rails will be installed inside the tunnels ready for the box jack itself - which NR intends to push into place during a nine-day engineering possession in September, following a trial push in late August. [...] A small number of weekday and weekend possessions will also be required on June 20-21, September 5-6, and between December 19-March 2021, [...]

glosses: Something that is owned.

examples.text: The car quickly became his most prized possession.
I would gladly give all of my worldly possessions just to be able to do that.

glosses: Ownership; taking, holding, keeping something as one's own.

examples.text: The car is in my possession.
I'm in possession of the car.

glosses: A territory under the rule of another country.

examples.text: Réunion is the largest of France's overseas possessions.

glosses: The condition or affliction of being possessed by a demon or other supernatural entity.

examples.text: Back then, people with psychiatric disorders were sometimes thought to be victims of demonic possession.
How long hath this possession held the man?

glosses: The condition of being under the control of strong emotion or madness.
Control of the ball; the opportunity to be on the offensive.

examples.text: The scoreboard shows a little football symbol next to the name of the team that has possession.

glosses: A disposal of the ball during a game, i.e. a kick or a handball.

glosses: A syntactic relationship between two nouns or nominals that may be used to indicate ownership.

examples.text: Some languages distinguish between a construction like 'my car', which shows alienable possession — the car could become someone else's — and one like 'my foot', which has inalienable possession — my foot will always be mine.

glosses: To invest with property.
The state of having complete legal control of something; possession; proprietorship.

examples.text: Other evidence of former ownerships such as notice-boards, number plates, and makers' plates, are often discovered unexpectedly. […] It has not been used for many years, and although it was impracticable to photograph the engine in the small confines of the shed it was possible to obtain a picture of the plate which it still carries showing the former ownership.
In the summer, DCC [Devon County Council] transferred ownership of the northern part of the station to NR for a nominal £1, enabling it (and the platform) to become part of the rail network.

glosses: Responsibility for or control over something.

examples.text: The successful candidate will take ownership of all internal design projects.

glosses: tatsächliche Sachherrschaft

examples.text: Dass der Besitz nach § 857 BGB auf den Erben übergeht, ist eine gesetzliche Fiktion.

„Körperliche, bewegliche Sachen werden durch physische Ergreifung, Wegführung oder Verwahrung; unbewegliche aber durch Betretung, Verrainung, Einzäunung, Bezeichnung oder Bearbeitung in Besitz genommen. In den Besitz unkörperlicher Sachen oder Rechte kommt man durch den Gebrauch derselben im eigenen Nahmen [sic!].“

glosses: Eigentum

examples.text: Das Fahrrad, das mir Ole gestohlen hat, ist nicht mehr in meinem Besitz.

glosses: das gesamte Eigentum einer Person

examples.text: Zum Besitz des Grafen gehören zwei Schlösser an der Loire, die schon seine Ahnen dem Verfall preisgaben.
